title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## HiFi-UMI: High-fidelity robot-free data enables zero-robot post-training of manipulation policies

### The Breakthrough
The authors introduce HiFi-UMI, a portable system that captures ultra‑wide‑FoV, microsecond‑synchronized robot‑free demonstrations with 3 mm end‑effector accuracy, building a 2,000‑hour dataset. Policies trained solely on this data reach up to 85% success on a precision insertion task, matching teleoperated baselines, and additional 4,000 hours of pre‑training further improve performance on unseen tasks.

### The Caveats
The experiments are confined to the same robot that recorded the data, with no cross‑hardware evaluation, so it remains unclear whether the learned policies truly generalize to other robots.

## SAM3D-Guided Object-Centric Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

### The Breakthrough
A frozen SAM3D model provides dense 3‑D object embeddings that are aligned to intermediate visual features of a VLA policy, allowing manipulation without depth or masks at test time. The method reports 99.1% success on the LIBERO benchmark and an average episode length of 4.11 on CALVIN, with real‑world gains in long‑horizon tasks.

### The Caveats
The paper reports high success rates but never compares against any existing VLA or object‑aware baselines, so it’s unclear whether the gains are due to the SAM3D alignment or other factors.

## S2A2: Audio‑Visual Imitation Learning for Manipulation Using Acoustic Spatial Cues

### The Breakthrough
S2A2 fuses visual features with acoustic spatial information (sound source direction) and spectral audio cues within a single imitation‑learning policy, enabling robots to locate and manipulate objects using sound. Experiments in simulation and on a real robot outperform existing policies on tasks that require both spatial positioning and timbre discrimination.

### The Caveats
The paper never ablates the visual‑only and audio‑only variants, so the reported gains could stem from the visual baseline alone and the contribution of acoustic cues remains unproven.

## Modular Robotic Catheters for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair

### The Breakthrough
The work presents a 2‑segment, 4‑DOF steerable catheter with an expandable tendon‑driven actuation platform, fabricated via thermal fiber drawing and laser micro‑machining; simulation and in‑vitro phantom tests demonstrate enhanced bending stiffness and steerability for fenestrated/branched endovascular aneurysm repair.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no quantitative comparison to existing catheters, so the claimed procedural‑time reduction and enhanced handling of complex cases remain unsubstantiated.

## Genki Robotics to launch first robot product and open OS to developers

### The Breakthrough
Genki Robotics plans to release its first consumer robot later this year and will open its operating system through an app‑store‑like marketplace, letting third‑party developers create, sell, and install robot behaviors to accelerate software innovation.

### The Caveats
The announcement offers no hardware prototypes, performance data, or real‑world testing, so the promised robot launch and open‑OS marketplace remain unverified.

## TurboFieldfare: Swift/Metal engine runs Gemma 4‑26B on M‑series Macs with 2 GB RAM

### The Breakthrough
TurboFieldfare is an open‑source Swift/Metal inference engine that streams 4‑bit quantized Gemma 4‑26B weights from SSD, keeping RAM usage around 2 GB on Apple silicon; it attains 5‑6 tok/s on an M2 Air and 31‑35 tok/s on an M5 Pro and includes an experimental OpenAI‑compatible local server.

### The Caveats
The demo provides no comparison to existing inference engines, so it’s unclear whether the claimed 2 GB RAM footprint and token‑per‑second speeds constitute a real improvement.

### Priority
HiFi-UMI is the most actionable breakthrough because it delivers a large, high‑quality dataset and demonstrates that manipulation policies can be trained without any post‑training robot runs.

### One action
Download the HiFi‑UMI dataset and evaluate your own manipulation policy on the provided benchmarks.

### What to watch
HiFi‑UMI, SAM3D‑guided VLA alignment, and S2A2 all pursue data‑centric or multimodal routes to improve robot manipulation—watch how quickly the community adopts high‑fidelity robot‑free demos, 3‑D object priors, and acoustic cues, and whether cross‑hardware validation emerges.
